lessons.title: Data Classes
lessons.content: A data class auto-generates equals(), hashCode(), toString(), copy(), and componentN() functions. Real scenario: your Lesson and Category domain models are perfect data class candidates.

codeSnippets.code:
data class User(val id: String, val name: String, val age: Int)
val user2 = user1.copy(age = 31)

lessons.title: Enum Classes
lessons.content: Defines a fixed set of named constant instances, which can hold their own properties/functions. Real scenario: a SyncStatus enum used in an exhaustive when block.

lessons.title: Sealed Classes
lessons.content: Restricts a type hierarchy to a known, closed set of subclasses, enabling exhaustive when handling. Real scenario: modeling API results as Success/Error/Loading instead of nullable fields.

lessons.title: Sealed Interfaces
lessons.content: Like sealed classes but as an interface, useful when subtypes also need to extend a different class. Real scenario: a UiState sealed interface where each variant is also a distinct domain type.

lessons.title: Value Classes (Inline Classes)
lessons.content: A value class wraps a single value in a type-safe wrapper optimized away at compile time in most cases. Real scenario: wrapping UserId and ProductId separately so the compiler prevents mixing them up.

lessons.title: Inline Classes (Historical Note)
lessons.content: 'inline class' was the original keyword before Kotlin 1.5 introduced 'value class' as the replacement. Real scenario: recognizing 'inline class' in older codebases as functionally the same as value class.

codeSnippets.code:
// old syntax, still valid but deprecated
inline class Password(val value: String)

lessons.title: Type Aliases
lessons.content: typealias gives an existing type a new, more descriptive name for readability - it doesn't create a new type. Real scenario: aliasing a verbose callback type like (Result<User>) -> Unit to UserCallback.
